historical_record.description: The main building went up between 1948 and 1952: six one-story, front-gabled volumes of light steel frame clad in stamped steel, erected as a pre-engineered Butler Building, a rigid-frame type common in the 1940s for utilitarian and military uses.

The structures have housed a radio shop, a machine shop, a paint shop, cable storage, a warehouse, a garage and offices, and the yard north of them was used for parking, traffic-signal storage and public-safety and telecommunications trailers; by 2011 the site held city offices, for the Department of Technology and the Municipal Transportation Agency.

unknowns: The produce-market environmental review dates the buildings here to 1948–1952 in its project description and cultural-resources chapter, but to 1948–1956 in its hazards chapter.
